claims.head: Sorokin doesn’t own the Oilers
claims.body: Sorokin has been a wall against the Oilers since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Sorokin isn’t that wall tonight.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Islanders have won two in a row, and the Oilers (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Wednesday. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Islanders fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 13th).

The Oilers’ record (.769) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.622), largely thanks to their finishing. So is the Islanders’ (.615 on chances worth .521), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Islanders (1st) and the Oilers (3rd) both get their defensemen shooting. The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest). The Islanders, by contrast, spread the ice time through the lineup (3rd). The Oilers also have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st), and that could do real damage against the Islanders’ penalty kill (30th), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way. Edmonton has scored 4.23 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Islanders have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Connor McDavid (8 G / 28 A / 36 P in 13 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with 13 points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 13 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games and seven goals in six games against the Islanders since 2023-24. Bo Horvat (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Isles’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.

Tristan Jarry (3-1-2 / .883 SV% in 6 GS) is expected to go for Edmonton. Ilya Sorokin (6-3-0 / .915 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and is expected to start. Sorokin has a .943 save percentage in five starts against the Oilers, well above his usual .906. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

Evan Bouchard has seven goals on chances worth about 2.8 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
